episodes.161696: Convection that developed over a portion of leeward Big Island was boosted by an upper low just north of the islands.  The rain caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.161725: On the evening of Monday September 27, 2021 showers in the area were quite active as a cool upper trough moved into the region. One storm cell produced an EF-0 tornado in Battle Ground, WA.
episodes.161776: Several supercell thunderstorms produced large hail across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.161839: Showers and thunderstorms developed early in the morning of September 28th across northern West Virginia due to a weak disturbance ahead of a cold front. As this line pushed southward into the northeast West Virginia mountains, a few became strong enough to produce instances of hail.
episodes.161899: An area of low pressure trekking over southwest Colorado was absorbed into a broader Pacific trough that lifted across the Western Slope. This led to scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to localized debris flows across portions of west-central Colorado over the course of a couple of days.
episodes.161934: A closed low located over northwestern New Mexico provided large scale lift to the region during the day on the 27th. After mostly light rain shower activity in the morning and early afternoon, skies cleared across the southwestern South Plains which allowed ample instability to develop. Thunderstorms erupted within this area of instability that had developed and moved eastward through the late afternoon and evening hours. Inverted-V soundings allowed these storms to produce several severe wind gusts.
episodes.162159: Showers and thunderstorms developed with the passage of a shortwave from the northwest. Low-level wind shear and instability helped enhance strong storm potential.
episodes.162334: A few showers and thunderstorms developed over eastern Pennsylvania on September 28 ahead of a cold front. Activity was isolated in nature and produced little impact overall. One storm in southeast Pennsylvania briefly became severe, before activity continued to weaken as it moved off to the east.
episodes.162502: A mid-level shortwave and a surface trough moved east over an unstable environment and were able to trigger strong storms over the coastal waters.
episodes.162564: The combination of near normal moisture, light steering winds from Hurricane Sam passing well northeast of the area, and local and diurnal effects resulted in active afternoons across portions of interior and western on September 28th and 29th.
episodes.163100: A cold front moving into a moderately unstable air mass produced an isolated severe thunderstorm in southern Rhode Island during the early afternoon.
episodes.163101: A cold front moving across the region triggered a few thunderstorms.  A lightning strike knocked down a tree and wires in southern Worcester County during the mid-morning.
episodes.163110: A microburst/heat burst process from anvil rainfall associated with weak storms in the area led to an isolated severe wind gust.
episodes.163119: A severe thunderstorm was nearly stationary for an hour near the community of Odem. Quarter sized hail occurred in Odem while power poles were blown down between Odem and Sinton.
episodes.163364: A low pressure system with multiple embedded disturbances moved across Arizona with scattered showers and thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.163405: A very moist air mass interacted with a passing upper disturbance. High rainfall rates and slow storm motion allowed flash flooding to occur.
episodes.163424: Strong thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding in Capitol Reef National Park.
episodes.163439: Gulf moisture surging into the local area pushed precipitable water values to above the 90th percentile for this time of year. At the same time, an upper level trough was digging into Texas. Showers and thunderstorms began developing ahead of this feature. A weak wind field in place was a prime environment for a slow moving storm to produce flash flooding.

events.narrative: A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Amherst measured severe wind gusts from 1853 through 1854 CST. A peak wind gust of 66 mph was measured at 1853 CST.
The automated surface observing system at Lubbock Preston Smith International Airport measured a severe wind gust of 61 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Abernathy measured severe wind gusts from 1958 through 2002 CST. A peak wind gust of 65 mph was measured at 2000 CST.

An EF-0 tornado with estimated winds of 85 mph (DI:28 ,DOD:3) began near the intersection of NE 72nd Avenue and State Highway 502 at 45.7804 latitude, -122.5982 longitude. The tornado tracked in a northeast direction, ending up near NE 259th St. and NE 147th Ave at 45.8105 latitude and -122.5229 longitude.  The tornado path was about 240 yards wide with a track length of about 3.9 miles. The estimated start and end time of the tornado is 1806PST and 1821PST.  No injuries or fatalities were reported. The majority of the damage was to trees that were uprooted or snapped. Other damage included a tree that fell on an RV, and fences damaged by toppled trees.
Kaibab National Forest reported that flooding closed Forest Road 22 from Forest Road 422A to Big Springs.
Slow moving heavy thunderstorm produced flooding at Fort Polk and along multiple roads in Vernon Parish. NWS equipment flooded at Fort Polk.
In Dudley, lightning knocked down a tree and wires on West Main Street.
In Cumberland, a thunderstorm produced dime size hail.
A few trees were reported to be blown down along Seneca Trail.
Multiple streets were flooded and impassable in Deridder.

In the Watch Hill section of Westerly, a wind gust to 62 mph was measured during a thunderstorm.
Heavy rain produced street flooding in South Lake Charles.
Flooding due to poor-drainage reported along Road PR-159 near Urbanization Brisas del Rio.
Mudslide reported on Road PR-111 near San Sebastian.
There were a couple reports of quarter size hail near Massanutten.
Golf ball size hail was reported in the 2000 block of Shady Acres Drive in Elkton.
Quarter size hail was reported near McMullen.
Quarter size hail was reported in Beldor.
Nickel to quarter size hail accumulated up to 2 inches deep just northeast of Stanardsville.

Flash flooding occurred in Capitol Gorge. The Scenic Drive was closed for over 24 hours due to flooding. Several vehicles were stuck, and required towing to be removed. Water and mud also flowed over state Route 24 east of the Hickman Bridge trailhead.
Quarter to ping pong ball size hail was reported just north of Earlysville.
Hail up to half dollar size was reported near Five Forks.
Burn scar debris flow from the Pine Gulch Fire flooded a house and rerouted Roan Creek at a bend 15 miles northwest of De Beque. Water marks along South Dry Fork Road were 3 to 6 feet high.
Up to golf ball size hail was reported near Rhoadsville.
Quarter to golf ball size hail was reported near Hollymead and Carrsbrook.
Veronica Drive in Chalmette was impassible due to high water.
Quarter size hail was reported just west of the Charlottesville city limits.
Media reported quarter sized hail occurred in Odem.
Power poles were snapped and a semi truck was blown over on Highway 77 between Sinton and Odem.
Shingles were blown off a roof and minor tree damage occurred in Upper Chichester Twp. Time estimated from radar.
